title: How to do Arnold curls
summary: Tutorial on a standing, bent-over concentration curl variation ("Arnold curls", after the Pumping Iron footage) that NH uses to hit the lower part of the biceps for the peak. He contrasts it with seated concentration curls, gives grip and setup cues, and recommends it as a tendon-friendly biceps finisher.

claims.claim: In Pumping Iron Arnold did concentration curls standing and bent over from the floor; most gym-goers do them seated instead.
Seated concentration curls are a good pump movement but tend to over-extend the shoulder, straining the rotator cuff and front delt, and they train the biceps generally rather than a specific region.
The Arnold curl variation emphasises the lower portion of the biceps, which helps create the peak when flexing, while still working the whole muscle.
Pick a dumbbell you can curl for 10-12 reps.
Grip: wrap the thumb around the handle, cup the dumbbell and let it sit very high in the palm; spread the legs, plant the elbow and curl at about a 45-degree angle.
Squeeze the biceps at the top and do not extend beyond that point; you will also feel the forearm working.
Keep it strict with no swinging; once the positive gets hard, help with the other hand on the lift and control the negative to squeeze out 1-2 extra reps.
The movement doesn't hurt the tendons, so it is a good biceps option when elbows are beaten up from lots of curls or chin-ups.
The variation is really an armwrestling exercise, but bodybuilding borrows any move that builds muscle; NH doubts Arnold actually did them this way.
